titolo: twitter Vulnerability Disclosure Program
descrizione: twitter public bug bounty program

scope: App mobile su Google Play / App Store
outOfScope: Attacchi DDoS / volumetrici
Social engineering su dipendenti
Test su ambienti di produzione con dati reali di utenti
Spam o invio massivo di contenuti
Vulnerabilità in browser di terze parti (es. Chrome bugs)
Rate limiting issues senza impatto reale
Self-XSS (richiede azione della vittima)
Vulnerabilità che richiedono accesso fisico al device
Clickjacking su pagine senza azioni sensibili
Best practice senza impatto dimostrabile
Username/email enumeration su form pubblici
CSRF su endpoint non state-changing
Vulnerabilità già note pubblicamente senza PoC aggiuntivo
Problemi di SPF/DKIM/DMARC
Mixed content warnings su pagine non autenticabili

testingTechniques.name: Ricognizione & Enumerazione
testingTechniques.description: Mappa tutte le superfici attaccabili, endpoint, sottodomini e tecnologie usate
steps: Esegui subdomain enumeration con subfinder, amass, assetfinder
Usa httpx per identificare servizi attivi
Fai crawling con katana o gospider per scoprire endpoint
Identifica tecnologie con Wappalyzer o whatweb
Leggi robots.txt, sitemap.xml, security.txt

testingTechniques.name: Test IDOR / BOLA
testingTechniques.description: Verifica controlli di accesso sostituendo ID utente/risorsa nelle API/URL
steps: Crea due account (A e B) sul programma
Identifica endpoint con ID numerici (/api/users/123, /orders/456)
Sostituisci ID di A con ID di B nelle richieste
Verifica se ricevi dati di B senza autorizzazione
Testa anche UUID e ID encoded in base64

testingTechniques.name: SQL Injection
testingTechniques.description: Testa parametri input per injection SQL classiche e blind
steps: Identifica parametri con sqlmap --crawl
Testa manualmente con payload base: apice, doppi apici, --, #
Usa sqlmap -u "URL" --dbs --batch per conferma
Testa anche blind SQL con time-based: ' OR SLEEP(5)--
Verifica second-order SQL injection in update profile

testingTechniques.name: XSS (Cross-Site Scripting)
testingTechniques.description: Inietta JavaScript in input riflessi o memorizzati
steps: Testa ogni parametro riflesso con: script alert 1 script
Verifica escaping di <, >, ", apice
Testa in attributi HTML con onmouseover
Usa event handler: img src x onerror alert 1
Testa stored XSS in campi profilo, commenti, recensioni

testingTechniques.name: SSRF (Server-Side Request Forgery)
testingTechniques.description: Forza il server a fare richieste verso risorse interne
steps: Identifica parametri URL: ?url=, ?image=, ?redirect=
Testa con 127.0.0.1, 169.254.169.254 (cloud metadata)
Bypassa filtri con localhost@evil.com, 0.0.0.0
Usa DNS rebinding con tools come singularity
Verifica accesso a metadata AWS/GCP/Azure

testingTechniques.name: Authentication Bypass
testingTechniques.description: Trova modi per bypassare login, OTP, 2FA
steps: Testa risposta su /api/login con credenziali vuote/invalide
Verifica rate limiting su OTP/2FA
Prova JWT manipulation: alg=none, alg=HS256 con public key
Testa password reset con token di un altro utente
Verifica session fixation e session hijacking

reportingSteps: 1. REGISTRAZIONE: Crea un account sul programma e metti il tuo handle di test in bio
2. RACCOLTA PROVE: Cattura screenshot/video di OGNI step della riproduzione con timestamp
3. MINIMIZZAZIONE: Crea un account demo e un account vittima (no dati reali)
4. REDAZIONE REPORT: Segui il template del programma, includi: Summary, Impact, Steps to Reproduce, PoC, Remediation
5. IMPATTO BUSINESS: Spiega sempre "What can an attacker do?" non solo "How does it work"
6. CVSS SCORE: Calcola il punteggio CVSS v3.1 con cvss calculator
7. SUBMIT: Carica su HackerOne/Bugcrowd/Intigriti e attendi triage (24-72h)
8. DUPLICATI: Se è un dup, è normale. Continua a cacciare!
9. RETEST: Dopo il fix, verifica che la patch funzioni davvero
10. DISCLOSURE: Aspetta il permesso del programma prima di blog/tweet
quickStartGuide: Step 1: Leggi TUTTO il policy del programma su twitter
Step 2: Configura Burp Suite con il proxy del tuo browser (FoxyProxy)
Step 3: Crea due account: attaccante e vittima su due browser diversi
Step 4: Mappa tutte le feature: signup, login, profilo, pagamenti, API
Step 5: Inizia con OWASP Top 10 e tools automatici (nuclei, sqlmap)
Step 6: Testa manualmente la business logic (sconti, ruoli, workflow)
Step 7: Documenta OGNI cosa interessante
Step 8: Scrivi un report chiaro con PoC riproducibile in 5 minuti
Step 9: Submeti e rispondi velocemente a domande del triage
Step 10: Studia i report pubblici (HackerOne Hacktivity) per imparare
tips: 💡 Leggi almeno 50 report risolti su HackerOne Hacktivity prima di iniziare
💡 Concentrati su UN programma per almeno 2 settimane
💡 Le business logic bug pagano DI PIÙ delle XSS
💡 I bug race condition sono sottovalutati ma pagati
💡 Usa Wayback Machine (web.archive.org) per trovare endpoint dimenticati
💡 Controlla sempre le API mobile vs web
💡 Non riportare MAI self-XSS, clickjacking senza impatto
💡 Impara Burp a livello avanzato: macro, match/replace, scanner
💡 La qualità del report > quantità
💡 Network: Discord Bugcrowd, NahamSec, InsiderPhD, STÖK

testingTechniques.name: Ricognizione & Enumerazione
testingTechniques.description: Mappa tutte le superfici attaccabili, endpoint, sottodomini e tecnologie usate
steps: Esegui subdomain enumeration con subfinder, amass, assetfinder
Usa httpx per identificare servizi attivi
Fai crawling con katana o gospider per scoprire endpoint
Identifica tecnologie con Wappalyzer o whatweb
Leggi robots.txt, sitemap.xml, security.txt

testingTechniques.name: Test IDOR / BOLA
testingTechniques.description: Verifica controlli di accesso sostituendo ID utente/risorsa nelle API/URL
steps: Crea due account (A e B) sul programma
Identifica endpoint con ID numerici (/api/users/123, /orders/456)
Sostituisci ID di A con ID di B nelle richieste
Verifica se ricevi dati di B senza autorizzazione
Testa anche UUID e ID encoded in base64

testingTechniques.name: SQL Injection
testingTechniques.description: Testa parametri input per injection SQL classiche e blind
steps: Identifica parametri con sqlmap --crawl
Testa manualmente con payload base: apice, doppi apici, --, #
Usa sqlmap -u "URL" --dbs --batch per conferma
Testa anche blind SQL con time-based: ' OR SLEEP(5)--
Verifica second-order SQL injection in update profile

testingTechniques.name: XSS (Cross-Site Scripting)
testingTechniques.description: Inietta JavaScript in input riflessi o memorizzati
steps: Testa ogni parametro riflesso con: script alert 1 script
Verifica escaping di <, >, ", apice
Testa in attributi HTML con onmouseover
Usa event handler: img src x onerror alert 1
Testa stored XSS in campi profilo, commenti, recensioni

testingTechniques.name: SSRF (Server-Side Request Forgery)
testingTechniques.description: Forza il server a fare richieste verso risorse interne
steps: Identifica parametri URL: ?url=, ?image=, ?redirect=
Testa con 127.0.0.1, 169.254.169.254 (cloud metadata)
Bypassa filtri con localhost@evil.com, 0.0.0.0
Usa DNS rebinding con tools come singularity
Verifica accesso a metadata AWS/GCP/Azure

testingTechniques.name: Authentication Bypass
testingTechniques.description: Trova modi per bypassare login, OTP, 2FA
steps: Testa risposta su /api/login con credenziali vuote/invalide
Verifica rate limiting su OTP/2FA
Prova JWT manipulation: alg=none, alg=HS256 con public key
Testa password reset con token di un altro utente
Verifica session fixation e session hijacking

testingTechniques.name: API Endpoint Discovery
testingTechniques.description: Mappa tutti gli endpoint API, parametri e metodi accettati
steps: Intercetta traffico con Burp Suite o OWASP ZAP
Usa kiterunner o wordlists API comuni
Testa metodi HTTP alternativi: PUT, DELETE, PATCH, OPTIONS
Verifica GraphQL introspection se presente
Leggi documentazione API pubblica su /docs, /swagger

testingTechniques.name: Mass Assignment
testingTechniques.description: Inietta campi non previsti nel body della richiesta
steps: Intercetta una richiesta PUT/POST normale
Aggiungi campi come: isAdmin true, role admin, verified true
Verifica se vengono accettati e modificano il tuo account
Testa con campi PII: ssn, creditCard, password
Prova con campi interni: internal_id, user_type

testingTechniques.name: Broken Object Level Authorization (BOLA)
testingTechniques.description: Accedi a oggetti di altri utenti cambiando ID
steps: Crea due account su due browser diversi
Cattura tutte le richieste con oggetti (es. /api/orders/123)
Sostituisci l'ID con uno dell'altro account
Se ottieni risposta 200 con dati altrui = BOLA confermato
Documenta sempre con screenshot prima/dopo

testingTechniques.name: Rate Limiting Bypass
testingTechniques.description: Bypassa limiti di velocità per brute force o scraping
steps: Identifica endpoint con rate limit (login, OTP, search)
Prova header X-Forwarded-For, X-Real-IP, X-Originating-IP
Cambia case del path: /API/Login vs /api/login
Aggiungi parametri irrilevanti: ?a=1&a=2
Usa IP rotation con proxy/VPN

testingTechniques.name: GraphQL Specific
testingTechniques.description: Testa vulnerabilità specifiche di GraphQL
steps: Abilita introspection con query: {__schema{types{name}}}
Usa batch query per rate limit bypass
Cerca field deprecated o hidden
Testa nested query DoS con depth limiting
Verifica authorization a livello di field, non solo oggetto

titolo: CVE-2026-100290: The regcomp and regexec functions in the GNU C Library version 2.3 to version 2.44 may read freed me...
descrizione:
The regcomp and regexec functions in the GNU C Library version 2.3 to version 2.44 may read freed memory and free the same heap block twice when a memory allocation fails while a regular expression is compiled or matched.  The re_dfa_add_node (the NFA node table) and build_range_exp (bracket ranges) grow several arrays with consecutive realloc calls and store the new pointers only after all of them succeed.  When a later call fails, the pattern buffer keeps pointers to blocks that were already freed, and the error cleanup frees them again.  In regexec, the back-reference cache (match_ctx_add_entry) frees its array when a realloc fails but keeps the pointer, which is freed again on the error path.

An attacker does not need to supply a crafted regular expression: patterns large enough to grow these arrays are common.  The failure has to hit a specific allocation, though, so the issue can only be reached when the system is already under memory pressure.  An attacker who supplies the pattern or the subject string has little control over which allocation fails, so the expected impact is a crash of the process.  This issue affects all architectures and ABIs supported by the GNU C Library.

titolo:
CVE-2026-105440: Missing authorization in the JSON-RPC web services interface
of Extreme Networks Switch Engine (EXOS...
descrizione:
Missing authorization in the JSON-RPC web services interface
of Extreme Networks Switch Engine (EXOS) allows an authenticated,
low-privileged (read-only) user to execute CLI show commands that are
restricted to that role through the command line interface. Successful
exploitation results in disclosure of sensitive information, including the
device configuration and the password hashes of local accounts. Configuration,
enable, and debug commands are not affected. Disclosed password hashes can be
attacked offline, and a weak password could lead to administrative access to
the device. This issue is fixed in Switch Engine 33.7.1-patch1-11,
33.1.100.133-patch1-9, and 32.7.4.15-patch1-11.








Extreme Networks would like to thank Toàn Lê (GitHub: https://github.com/toanln-cov) for responsibly disclosing this vulnerability and for working with our PSIRT team through coordinated disclosure.

titolo: CVE-2026-115819: Calling the wide scanf family of functions (swscanf, fwscanf, wscanf, vswscanf, vfwscanf and vwscanf...
descrizione:
Calling the wide scanf family of functions (swscanf, fwscanf, wscanf, vswscanf, vfwscanf and vwscanf) with a %s or %[ conversion without the 'l' length modifier in the GNU C Library version 2.2 to version 2.44 writes an extra null byte one past the end of the destination array when the converted multibyte string and its terminating null byte exactly fill that array.

These conversions store each wide input character into the caller's char array as a multibyte sequence.  The conversion ends with the sequence that returns to the initial shift state, which also stores the terminating null byte, and the functions then append a second null byte.  A destination sized for the converted string and one terminator, as the C standard requires the caller to provide, is therefore written one byte past its end.  The out-of-bounds byte is always a null byte, which may corrupt adjacent data or crash the process.  An attacker who supplies the input can trigger the overflow with a string whose converted length exactly fills the destination.

The narrow scanf functions, the %ls and %l[ conversions into a wchar_t array, and the 'a' and 'm' allocation modifiers are not affected, and storing a wide scanf conversion into a narrow char array is uncommon.  This issue affects all architectures and ABIs supported by the GNU C Library.

titolo: CVE-2026-64855: soapbar is a SOAP library for Python — client, server, and WSDL handling. Prior to version 0.13.0, v...
descrizione: soapbar is a SOAP library for Python — client, server, and WSDL handling. Prior to version 0.13.0, verify_envelope_bsp() derived its trust anchor from the message it was verifying. It read the X.509 certificate out of the caller-untrusted wsse:BinarySecurityToken, validated only that certificate's not-before / not-after dates, and then verified the signature against that same certificate. There was no CA-chain validation, no issuer/subject allowlist, and no pinning. A successful verify_envelope_bsp() therefore proved only that the envelope was signed by whoever supplied the embedded certificate — never that it was signed by a trusted party. An attacker who mints their own certificate, signs a forged envelope, and embeds that certificate in the token passes verification. Any consumer that treats a successful BSP verification as authentication can be impersonated (signature forgery / authentication bypass). verify_envelope() (which pins a caller-supplied x509_cert) was not affected — the flaw was specific to the BSP variant whose trust anchor came from the message. This issue has been patched in version 0.13.0.

titolo: CVE-2026-119233: proxygen's HTTP/3 codec buffered an incomplete non-DATA frame, such as a control-stream frame, a fra...
descrizione: proxygen's HTTP/3 codec buffered an incomplete non-DATA frame, such as a control-stream frame, a frame of an unknown or reserved type, or a HEADERS frame, until its entire declared length had arrived, without limiting that length, and re-scanned all buffered data each time more bytes arrived. A remote, unauthenticated HTTP/3 peer could declare a very large frame and deliver it slowly, causing unbounded memory growth and CPU usage that grows quadratically with the number of fragments, leading to denial of service. This issue affects proxygen versions prior to v2026.11.09.00.

titolo: CVE-2026-119234: mvfst did not adequately merge or compact out-of-order STREAM frame data, and a small received fragm...
descrizione: mvfst did not adequately merge or compact out-of-order STREAM frame data, and a small received fragment could keep a much larger receive buffer alive. QUIC flow control limits the number of buffered stream bytes, but not this per-fragment memory and bookkeeping. A remote, unauthenticated QUIC peer could send many small, non-contiguous stream fragments to make an endpoint consume memory far in excess of its advertised receive window and spend increasing CPU time reassembling stream data, leading to denial of service. This issue affects mvfst versions prior to v2026.11.09.0.

titolo: CVE-2026-119235: proxygen's QPACK decoder enforced its size limit on a string literal in an encoder-stream instructio...
descrizione: proxygen's QPACK decoder enforced its size limit on a string literal in an encoder-stream instruction only after the entire literal had been received. A remote, unauthenticated HTTP/3 peer could send an insert instruction on the QPACK encoder stream that declares an arbitrarily large literal and then keep sending data, causing the decoder to buffer it without bound for the lifetime of the connection and exhaust memory, leading to denial of service. titolo: CVE-2026-119236: An mvfst QUIC server retained CRYPTO frame data received at an encryption level (Initial or Handshak...
descrizione: An mvfst QUIC server retained CRYPTO frame data received at an encryption level (Initial or Handshake) that the TLS handshake had already moved past. Because the transport treated this data as delivered, it did not count against the CRYPTO stream buffer limit. A remote, unauthenticated client could complete a handshake, withhold its acknowledgment of the server's HANDSHAKE_DONE frame so that Handshake keys stay in use, and keep sending Handshake-level CRYPTO data at increasing offsets, causing unbounded memory growth on the server and leading to denial of service. This issue affects mvfst versions prior to v2026.11.09.00.

titolo: GHSA-x2vm-cf3p-m2w8: libp2p: gossipsub creates a permanent topics-map entry per distinct subscription with no cap in the default config
descrizione:
### Summary
A single gossipsub peer can grow a node's `topics` map without bound by flooding subscription RPCs, because the default configuration has no global, per-peer, or topic-length cap and peer scoring does not penalise subscription volume. The peer is never greylisted, so the growth continues toward OOM.

### Details
`handleReceivedSubscription` (`packages/gossipsub/src/gossipsub.ts:1028`, line 1036) runs `this.topics.set(topic, new Set())` for every distinct topic string:

```ts
private handleReceivedSubscription (from, topic, subscribe) {
  let topicSet = this.topics.get(topic)
  if (subscribe) {
    if (topicSet == null) {
      topicSet = new Set()
      this.topics.set(topic, topicSet)   // no global cap, no per-peer cap
    }
    topicSet.add(from.toString())
  }
}
```

The only topical gate (`gossipsub.ts:981`, `if (this.allowedTopics != null && !this.allowedTopics.has(topic)) return`) is skipped when `allowedTopics` is null — the default. Subscriptions are unsigned RPC metadata (no signature needed); `decodeRpc`'s per-RPC limit caps count (`maxSubscriptions = 5000`) but not topic-string length or aggregate size; and the peer-scoring components P1–P7 have no subscription-volume term, so the attacker's score stays at 0 (above the `graylistThreshold` of −80) and `acceptFrom` keeps returning true. Verified on js-libp2p commit `a04f5e0`, where `@libp2p/gossipsub` reads `16.0.4`.

### PoC
Full PoC attached (`gossipsub-topics-unbounded-growth-poc.tar.gz`). Build the js-libp2p monorepo at the affected version (`npm install --ignore-scripts && npm run build`), extract the package inside the monorepo root (sibling of `packages/`), then `cd gossipsub-topics-unbounded-growth-poc && node attack.mjs`. Expected (default config):

```
[*] sending 300 RPC frames x 4000 unique ~190-byte topic subscriptions (1,200,000 topics total)
[*]   progress: 88% sent | victim topics=1,032,000 rss=740MB peers=1
[*] victim quiesced: topics=~1,100,000 rss=~870MB peers=1
[!] Vulnerability reproduced: one connected peer grew the victim's gossipsub topics map to ~1.1M entries (RSS +~900MB) with 300 subscription RPCs — no global, per-peer, or topic-length cap in the default config
```

Control run (`ALLOWED_TOPICS=legit-topic`, i.e. `node attack.mjs control`): the identical flood is rejected at the `allowedTopics` gate and the topics map stays at 0 entries — confirming the vulnerable condition is the default `allowedTopics`-unset config. The map grows monotonically with no cap until the victim's own resource pressure trips; on disconnect `removePeer` performs an O(N) sweep over every topic entry (a secondary CPU cost) while the ~1 GB heap stays committed.

### Impact
CWE-400/CWE-770. Every node running default gossipsub is affected; the attacker needs only one connection and is never rate-limited or greylisted. Growth continues toward OOM; on disconnect the O(N) `removePeer` sweep adds CPU cost. Suggested fix: bound by default (not opt-in) — a global cap on `topics.size`, a per-peer subscription cap with a P7 behaviour penalty so `acceptFrom` eventually greylists, a topic-string length cap at decode time, and/or flipping `allowedTopics` to deny-by-default; make `removePeer`'s topic iteration non-blocking/capped.

[gossipsub-topics-unbounded-growth-poc.tar.gz](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/30452451/gossipsub-topics-unbounded-growth-poc.tar.gz)

titolo: GHSA-rvfr-cqwq-rc4j: libp2p: ASN.1 DER decoder drives an unbounded synchronous loop on attacker-controlled length fields, stalling the Node event loop pre-auth
descrizione:
### Summary
A remote peer can stall a js-libp2p node's entire event loop for ~4–5 seconds per connection (and transiently allocate ~2 GB) by sending a ~15-byte crafted `publicKey` inside an Identify message. The malformed key reaches the DER decoder before any peer-id/signature check, so the attack is pre-auth and repeatable indefinitely by reconnecting.

### Details
`packages/crypto/src/keys/rsa/der.ts` `readLength()` parses DER long-form lengths with no comparison to `buf.byteLength`, and `readInteger()` then loops over the attacker-claimed length:

```ts
function readInteger (buf, context) {
  const length = readLength(buf, context)   // attacker-controlled, claims up to 2^64
  const end = context.offset + length
  for (let i = context.offset; i < end; i++) // runs far past buf.byteLength
    vals.push(buf[i])                         // pushes `undefined` past the end
}
```

The blob reaches the parser pre-auth: Identify runs on every `connection:open` and calls `publicKeyFromProtobuf(publicKey)` (`packages/protocol-identify/src/identify.ts:85`) before the `connection.remotePeer.equals(id)` check at `identify.ts:88`. The `MAX_RSA_JWK_SIZE` guard in `pkixToRSAPublicKey` only bounds the total blob size, not the inner length field, so a 15-byte payload defeats it; the ECDSA path (`unmarshalECDSAPublicKey`) has no cap at all. The decode runs in a single synchronous tick, so no `AbortSignal` — including Identify's 5 s timeout — can interrupt it. Verified on js-libp2p commit `a04f5e0`, where `@libp2p/crypto` reads `5.1.21`.

### PoC
Full PoC attached (`libp2p-crypto-der-eventloop-dos-poc.tar.gz`). Build the js-libp2p monorepo at the affected version (`npm install --ignore-scripts && npm run build`), extract the package inside the monorepo root (sibling of `packages/`), then `cd libp2p-crypto-der-eventloop-dos-poc && node attack.mjs`. Expected:

```
[*] round 1: payload sent=true, victim event-loop stall = 4s, peak RSS ~1980 MB
[*] round 2: payload sent=true, victim event-loop stall = 4-5s, peak RSS ~1980 MB
[*] round 3: payload sent=true, victim event-loop stall = 4s, peak RSS ~1980 MB
[!] Vulnerability reproduced: 3/3 connections each stalled the victim's event loop for ~4-5s — one crafted ~15-byte Identify publicKey per connection, pre-auth
```

The stall is measured from the victim's own 1 s heartbeat clock (frozen while the loop is blocked); the ~2 GB transient RSS peak is read from `/proc/<pid>/status`. The DER `RangeError` is swallowed by Identify's `.catch(() => {})`, so the node survives and every new connection re-stalls it; under a container memory limit the ~2 GB spike OOM-kills the process. A `node attack.mjs control` run (legitimate Identify) shows 0 s stalls.

### Impact
CWE-130/CWE-400. Any node running the default Identify service is affected. A single peer can keep the node unresponsive to all of its peers (every new connection adds another multi-second stall — all timers, heartbeats, and protocol timeouts stop) and, in memory-constrained deployments, force an OOM kill. Suggested fix: in `readLength`, reject any long-form length whose value exceeds `buf.byteLength - context.offset`; in `readInteger`/`readObjectIdentifier`/`readBitString`/`readOctetString`, clamp or assert `end`/`finalOffset` against `buf.byteLength` before looping; add an overall DER-element-length sanity cap at `decodeDer` entry and a byte-length cap in `unmarshalECDSAPublicKey`.

[libp2p-crypto-der-eventloop-dos-poc.tar.gz](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/30452369/libp2p-crypto-der-eventloop-dos-poc.tar.gz)

titolo: GHSA-828w-6qgx-3rcf: Filament Curator: Cross-tenant media metadata disclosure via Curator picker search
descrizione:
Summary

  In multitenant Filament panels, an authenticated user could retrieve media metadata belonging to other tenants
  by typing in the Curator media-picker search box. The search query omitted the tenant ownership scope that the
  normal file listing applies.

  Details

  CuratorPanel::updatedSearch() built its Eloquent query independently of getFiles() and did not apply the
  filament()->hasTenancy() && $isTenantAware tenant-ownership where clause. As a result, the search matched media
  across all tenants. A secondary flaw compounded it: the orWhere('title'…) chain was not wrapped in a nested
  group, so the OR conditions also broke out of the isLimitedToDirectory constraint.

  The issue was introduced in v3.2.4, when multitenancy support was added to the media picker.

  Impact

  - Who: any authenticated user with access to a panel that uses the Curator picker.
  - What: disclosure of other tenants' media metadata (name, title, alt, caption, description, path, etc.)
  returned by the search.
  - Conditions: only affects deployments using Filament multitenancy with Curator's tenant awareness enabled.
  Single-tenant installs are not affected.

  Patches

titolo: GHSA-xhv5-8fpq-g7hf: qbee-agent: Local Privilege Escalation and Arbitrary File Tampering via Symlink Following in createFile helper
descrizione:
This is a Local Privilege Escalation (LPE) vulnerability stemming from improper symlink handling (CWE-59: Link Following) and improper ownership management (CWE-282) inside the qbee-agent file manager logic.

### Impact

Any managed device running qbee-agent up to the affected versions. The impact manifests in three distinct vectors:

1. **Primary Vector (Full Privilege Escalation to Root - Default Configuration)**: If an unprivileged user's account is managed by the SSH Keys bundle, they can replace or remove their own `~/.ssh` directory and create a symlink pointing to `/root/.ssh`. On the next configuration apply, qbee-agent follows the symlink and writes the user's server-provisioned public key directly into `/root/.ssh/authorized_keys`. Since the symlink resides inside the user's own home directory, kernel protections like `fs.protected_symlinks` do not block this execution. The attacker can then instantly log in as root via SSH.

2. **Secondary Vector (Arbitrary File Overwrite / DoS via RAUC Staging)**: On devices utilizing RAUC download mode, the agent uses a predictable, world-writable staging path (`/tmp/.bundle.raucb.part`). If `fs.protected_symlinks` is disabled `(0)`, an unprivileged user can symlink this path to a vital system file (e.g., `/etc/shadow` or `/etc/pam.d/*`), causing the agent to truncate or overwrite it with server-supplied update data during a RAUC update deployment.

3. **Tertiary Vector (Arbitrary File Re-ownership via File Distribution)**: If an operator configures a file-distribution/template destination under a directory owned by an unprivileged user, the attacker can create a symlink at the partial download path targeting a sensitive system file. The agent will then inadvertently execute `file.Chown()` on the targeted file, handing ownership over to the unprivileged attacker.

### Patches

The vulnerability has been addressed by hardening file creation and directory traversal inside `app/configuration/file_manager.go`. Specifically, the agent now enforces `syscall.O_NOFOLLOW` and proper existence validation flags during privileged operations to prevent link resolution outside intended directories.

Users should upgrade to version 2026.27 (or newer) to fully mitigate these vectors.

### Workarounds

If upgrading immediately is not feasible, administrators can apply the following mitigations:

1. Disable the SSH Keys Bundle: Temporarily turn off SSH key management within the Qbee platform for non-trusted local accounts to eliminate the primary privilege escalation vector.

2. Restrict Local Home Directory Alterations: Enforce strict file permissions or monitoring on managed user home directories to block unprivileged users from deleting or replacing ~/.ssh with a symbolic link.

3. Enable Kernel Symlink Protection: Ensure that system-level symlink protections are active to mitigate the secondary `/tmp` vector by verifying that the following sysctl parameter is set to 1 (though note this does not fix the primary home directory vector):

```bash
sysctl -w fs.protected_symlinks=1
```

titolo: GHSA-c5q4-97jw-jggh: AWS-advanced-jdbc-wrapper: Java Deserialization RCE via Cache Poisoning
descrizione:
### Impact
The AWS Advanced JDBC Wrapper is an open-source JDBC driver wrapper that extends a JDBC driver to enable Amazon Aurora and AWS Cloud features such as failover handling and caching. We identified CVE-2026-14265, an issue in the RemoteQueryCachePlugin of the AWS Advanced JDBC Wrapper. When this plugin is enabled, query results read from the shared Redis/Valkey cache are deserialized without class filtering. An actor with write access to the shared cache infrastructure could insert a crafted serialized Java object that, when read by an application, results in execution of arbitrary code on the application server.

### Workarounds
The RemoteQueryCachePlugin is not enabled by default. Customers who cannot immediately upgrade can mitigate this issue by disabling the RemoteQueryCachePlugin, and by restricting write access to the Redis/Valkey cache infrastructure to trusted principals.

titolo: GHSA-v858-xh7w-8jr5: pympp allows excessive sponsored transaction fees through padded calldata
descrizione:
### Details
When the server acts as the fee_payer, `pympp` 0.8.0 validates calldata using `eth_abi` decoding, which is lenient about trailing bytes. The `FeePayerPolicy` caps `gas_limit` (≤ 2 M) and `max_fee_per_gas` (≤ 100 Gwei) but does **not** check calldata length.

Tempo uses legacy calldata gas pricing: **16 gas per non-zero byte**. Appending `N` bytes of `0x01` padding inflates actual gas used by `N × 16` while keeping `gas_limit` and `max_fee_per_gas` within policy caps. The server cosigns and broadcasts the padded transaction, draining its fee-payer wallet.

**Vulnerable code path:** `FeePayerPolicy` in `fee_payer_policy.py` (pympp 0.8.0) enforces `maxGas = 2_000_000` and `maxFeePerGas = 100 Gwei` but has no `calldata.length` bound. The policy check passes because the inflated gas comes from intrinsic calldata cost, not the declared `gas_limit`.

**Note:** In our experiment, we enforce an 16 KB `max_header_length`, which caps the maximum effective padding at roughly 5,500 bytes. The default padding in this PoC (5,500 bytes) is within that limit.

### PoC
The PoC is provided below. It is configured to reproduce the attack on Tempo Moderate testnet within a Docker environment. Download the PoC and run:
```bash
unzip pympp_python_PoC.zip
cd pympp_python
docker build -t pympp-padding .
docker run --rm pympp-padding
``` 
There are more details in `pympp_python/README.md`

### Impact
In our experiment, a malicious client can force the server to pay ~**5x** the normal transaction fee. This dramatically increases operational costs and completely destroys the profit margin on low-cost items.

Please provide a way to share the PoC in .zip format to you. Thank you!

titolo: GHSA-gfv3-m769-5xm3: Phoenix: Format String Injection in applyChatTemplate
descrizione: - Summary A format string injection vulnerability in the applyChatTemplate GraphQL endpoint allows an attacker to read server-side environment variables, cryptographic secrets, and internal module attributes directly from the API response. On default Phoenix installations where authentication is disabled the endpoint is reachable with no credentials. On auth-enabled deployments, any account regardless of privilege level is sufficient to exploit it. - Impact Server filesystem paths, loaded Python module names, and internal configuration constants are fully disclosed, an attacker with network access can read the full server `os.environ` including the admin credentials hardcoded in `phoenix.auth`. Successful exploitation allows an attacker to extract PHOENIX_SECRET, the master key used to sign all JWTs and derive the Fernet encryption key protecting stored credentials (LLM API keys, OAuth tokens). With this key, an attacker can forge admin-level session tokens and decrypt all secrets stored in the database. - Affected Versions First vulnerable release: arize-phoenix-v13.0.0 (2026-02-13) Latest confirmed vulnerable release: arize-phoenix-v14.8.0 (2026-04-17) - Affected Component `applyChatTemplate` GraphQL query endpoint (`src/phoenix/server/api/queries.py:1638`) `FStringTemplateFormatter._format()` template rendering function (`src/phoenix/utilities/template_formatters.py:272`) `DotDict.__getattr__()` ineffective attribute access control (`src/phoenix/utilities/template_formatters.py:90`) - Proof of Concept payload as txt with an image performing the exploit below. - Payload: ``` { "query": "query($t: PromptChatTemplateInput!, $o: PromptTemplateOptions!) { applyChatTemplate(template: $t, templateOptions: $o) { messages { content { ... on TextContentPart { text { text } } } } } }", "variables": { "t": { "messages": [{ "role": "USER", "content": [{ "text": { "text": "{u.__class__.__bases__[0].__init__.__globals__[_os].environ}" } }] }] }, "o": { "format": "F_STRING", "variables": { "u": { "x": 1 } } } } } ``` - Suggested Fix Three mitigations are recommended in combination: restrict attribute traversal at the Formatter.get_field() level (not the wrapper class), add IsAuthenticated permission to the applyChatTemplate resolver, and limit F_STRING format to trusted system-defined templates only. Best Regards, Omar

titolo: GHSA-vc7v-qv4w-wrv8: Next.js: Cache leak across root param values in nested 'use cache' functions via delayed inner stream metadata
descrizione:
With Cache Components enabled, an outer `'use cache'` function can be keyed incorrectly even when its inner `'use cache'` call generates a fresh entry. If the inner function reads a root param (via `next/root-params`) and returns a value that still contains pending promises — for example an object with data that is ready immediately alongside slower data — React Flight delivers the ready portion to the outer function before the inner entry has finished publishing its root param dependencies. The outer function can then finish, and its cache entry is persisted under a key that omits that root param. The entry is written once and reused for all root param values, so a response for one root param value can serve content produced for a different value. Entries written this way can also ignore tag invalidation and cache lifetimes of the nested caches they consumed.

What values are leaked cannot be attacker controlled. Which value's content is served depends only on which invocation wrote the entry first.

This is a variant of https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-h694-7cp9-m8p3 that the fix for that advisory does not cover: it does not require the inner call to be served from an existing entry, and it does not depend on a slow cache handler.

titolo: GHSA-vx32-xf7g-9ghr: qbee-agent: Docker Compose build context Zip Slip writes outside context directory
descrizione:
## Summary

`qbee-agent` contains a Zip Slip vulnerability in `app/utils/tar.go`. The tar extractor checks whether an entry remains inside the destination directory with:

```go
strings.HasPrefix(targetPath, destdirClean)
```

This does not enforce a path separator boundary. If the destination directory is `/tmp/.../context`, a tar entry such as `../context-outside/payload.txt` cleans to `/tmp/.../context-outside/payload.txt` and still passes the prefix check. qbee-agent then creates the outside directory and writes the payload outside the intended extraction root.

The issue is reachable through the Docker Compose build context path when `UseContext` is enabled.

## Details

Code references below were verified against `qbee-io/qbee-agent` commit:

- `1d8bdbb7422adb4ca563d3114cbe2817d6ba3581`

Affected repository:

- `qbee-io/qbee-agent`

Affected files:

- `app/utils/tar.go`
- Docker Compose context path in `app/configuration/bundle_docker_compose.go`

The vulnerable extraction code:

- `app/utils/tar.go:89-93`

```go
targetPath := filepath.Clean(filepath.Join(destPath, header.Name))
destdirClean := filepath.Clean(destPath)

if !strings.HasPrefix(targetPath, destdirClean) {
    return fmt.Errorf("tar entry %s is outside of destination directory %s", targetPath, destdirClean)
}
```

The file is then created at the accepted `targetPath`:

- `app/utils/tar.go:96-109`

```go
case tar.TypeDir:
    if err := os.MkdirAll(targetPath, 0755); err != nil {
        return err
    }
case tar.TypeReg:
    targetFile, err := os.Create(targetPath)
```

Docker Compose build contexts reach this extractor:

- `app/configuration/bundle_docker_compose.go:238-270`

The context archive is downloaded and then unpacked into the compose project context directory with `utils.UnpackTar`.

Archive source and role evidence:

- `app/configuration/compose.go:14` defines the Docker Compose build context as the remote configuration field `Context string`.
- `app/configuration/compose.go:26` enables this path with `UseContext`.
- `app/configuration/file_manager.go:240-246` and `app/configuration/file_manager.go:281-287` show that context sources are resolved either from `file://` local files or from the Qbee file-manager API.
- Qbee's Docker Compose documentation lists "Build Context" as a Docker Compose configuration option: https://docs.qbee.io/configuration-docker-compose.html
- Qbee's RBAC documentation separates `configuration:manage` from `files:manage`, and maps "Configure -> Modify configuration" to `configuration:manage` while "Files manager -> Write access" maps to `files:manage`: https://docs.qbee.io/account-users-and-roles.html
- Qbee's CI/CD documentation describes using a dedicated Qbee user with a role restricted to configuration changes to push and commit deployment configuration: https://docs.qbee.io/tutorial-iot-container-deployment-with-ci-cd-devops.html

Trust-boundary requirement:

- The vulnerable primitive is clear: qbee-agent writes a regular file outside the intended context extraction directory.
- The security boundary is present when the archive supplier is less privileged than the local qbee-agent process and is not supposed to write arbitrary sibling files in qbee-agent's Docker Compose cache/project area.
- The public code and documentation support this boundary for tenants that delegate configuration and/or file-manager access to limited users or CI automation.
- If a deployment allows only full device/fleet administrators to provide Docker Compose context archives, the finding should be treated as hardening for that deployment.

## PoC

Two failing regression tests add.

The utility-level test proves the extractor bug directly:

- `app/utils/tar_test.go:132`
- `Test_TarZipSlipSiblingPrefixBypass`

Command:

```sh
wsl -e sh -lc 'cd /mnt/c/Users/kwak0/Documents/Qbee/targets/qbee-agent; /mnt/c/Users/kwak0/Documents/Qbee/.tools/go1.26.4-linux/go/bin/go test ./app/utils -run Test_TarZipSlipSiblingPrefixBypass -count=1 -v'
```

Observed result:

```text
=== RUN   Test_TarZipSlipSiblingPrefixBypass
    tar_test.go:169: expected unpackTar to reject sibling-prefix traversal archive
    tar_test.go:174: path traversal: payload was written outside destPath at /tmp/.../context-outside/payload.txt; got "zip-slip-sibling-prefix"
--- FAIL: Test_TarZipSlipSiblingPrefixBypass (0.00s)
FAIL
```

The Docker Compose bundle-path test proves reachability through `Compose.getContext()`:

- `app/configuration/bundle_docker_compose_context_zip_slip_test.go:13`
- `Test_ComposeContextRejectsSiblingPrefixZipSlip`

Command:

```sh
wsl -e sh -lc 'cd /mnt/c/Users/kwak0/Documents/Qbee/targets/qbee-agent; /mnt/c/Users/kwak0/Documents/Qbee/.tools/go1.26.4-linux/go/bin/go test ./app/configuration -run Test_ComposeContextRejectsSiblingPrefixZipSlip -count=1 -v'
```

Observed result:

```text
=== RUN   Test_ComposeContextRejectsSiblingPrefixZipSlip
    bundle_docker_compose_context_zip_slip_test.go:66: expected compose context unpack to reject sibling-prefix traversal archive
    bundle_docker_compose_context_zip_slip_test.go:75: compose context path traversal wrote outside context dir at /tmp/.../cache/docker_compose/project-a/context-outside/payload.txt; got "compose-context-zip-slip"
--- FAIL: Test_ComposeContextRejectsSiblingPrefixZipSlip (0.00s)
FAIL
```

## Impact

An attacker-controlled Docker Compose build context archive can create directories and regular files outside qbee-agent's intended context extraction directory, with qbee-agent process privileges.

The demonstrated impact is constrained path traversal:

- It can write sibling-prefix paths such as `cache/docker_compose/<project>/context-outside/payload.txt`.
- It does not demonstrate writing arbitrary paths such as `/etc/passwd`; those do not pass the current string-prefix check.
- It can corrupt or alter files in nearby qbee-agent Docker Compose cache/project paths if their cleaned path shares the destination prefix.
- It may affect integrity or availability of qbee-agent-managed Docker Compose state, depending on the project/cache layout.

This report does not claim direct RCE.

titolo: GHSA-c94f-87xg-65wf: Silverstripe Framework: RCE via i18nTextCollectorTask writer parameter
descrizione:
### Impact
The writer option of the i18nTextCollectorTask dev task was passed to the injector without validation. A crafted dev task URL could create arbitrary objects with attacker-controlled constructor arguments and run code on the server. Because the dev task did not ask for confirmation, an administrator could be tricked into running it by following a link. On a site in dev mode, no login was needed. CMS 5 is not affected.

### Reported by
Jack Wallace

titolo: GHSA-7h45-q5jx-7r87: Directus: Share update allows reassigning user_created and role
descrizione:
### Summary

A non-admin user who can update their own shares can reassign a share's creator (`user_created`), `role`, `item`, and `collection` fields after the share is created. The update is authorized against the row as it existed before the change, and the resulting row is never revalidated, so these fields can be set to values the user would not be permitted to assign when creating a share. By reassigning both `user_created` and `role` to an administrator the share's effective permissions get elevated.

This is a server-side authorization gap in the share update path. It does not by itself produce an administrator token. It re-opens a previously patched privilege-escalation surface on the effective permissions of a share.

### Prerequisites

- An authenticated non-admin account that holds update permission on `directus_shares`. This is not part of the baseline app-access grant, which is read-only on a user's own shares, but it is part of the recommended defaults permission template for `directus_shares` that instances commonly apply so the share feature is usable.
- An item the account is allowed to share.
- Knowledge of an administrator user and role identifier to assign. In the reported case these were read from a relation on the shareable item using ordinary read permissions.

### Details

The recommended default permission for updating `directus_shares` selects rows where the caller is the creator and permits writes to the full field set, including the creator, role, item, and collection. The ownership filter is evaluated only against the row as it exists before the update, so an owned share passes the check. The merged row is never re-checked to decide whether the caller may assign the new values.

Two guards that are enforced when a share is created are absent on update. On create, the creator is forced to the acting user, and a share-access check is run against the target item to confirm the caller is allowed to share it. On update, the supplied creator value is stored as given and no equivalent share-access check is run against the new item or collection, so both the creator and the shared target can be repointed to values the caller was never authorized to set. The read-only marking on the creator field in the schema is a Data Studio UI hint and does not constrain writes through the API.

When a guest authenticates through the share, Directus derives one accountability from the share's creator and another from the share's role, and applies administrator reach only when both resolve to an administrator. After both fields are reassigned to an administrator, both inputs resolve to administrator and the share is evaluated with full-schema reach starting from the shared item. This is the bypass of the CVE-2025-24353 intersection, which assumed the creator and selected role remain trustworthy after creation, when in fact both are mutable together through update.

### Impact

Improper authorization (CWE-863) and improper privilege management (CWE-269). A non-admin can raise the effective permissions of a share they own beyond both their own permissions and the share role's permissions, exposing data reachable from the shared item that neither principal should be able to expose. The direct impact is to confidentiality. This issue alone does not grant write or availability impact.

titolo: GHSA-8cgq-x343-p74c: mail-parser: One hostile attachment aborts `write_attachments()` and silently drops the rest of the batch
descrizione:
### Impact

`write_attachments()` called `_safe_attachment_filename()` and `write_sample()` inside its loop
with no guard, so a single crafted attachment raised out of the whole save. Every attachment
**after** the malicious one was silently never written, with no error surfaced to a caller that
catches only `MailParserError`.

That is an evasion primitive as much as an availability bug: a sender puts one poisoned part
first and the real payload second, and the payload never reaches the extraction directory that
a downstream scanner or sandbox reads — while it still reaches the recipient's mail client
intact. The tool's output diverges from the bytes actually in the message, which is the same
failure mode as the filename-sanitizing bypass in
[GHSA-fr3h-cpq2-9496](https://github.com/SpamScope/mail-parser/security/advisories/GHSA-fr3h-cpq2-9496).

Three shapes were reachable, all from attacker-controlled MIME metadata:

- **NUL smuggled through RFC 2231** — `filename*=us-ascii''evil%00.bin` decodes to a NUL in the
  filename during parsing and raised `ValueError` out of the name check;
- **overlong basename** — a filename longer than `NAME_MAX` (e.g. 300 characters) raised
  `OSError: File name too long` from `open()`, *after* creating a zero-byte stub on disk;
- **undecodable payload** — a body that is not valid base64 raised `binascii.Error` (a
  `ValueError` subclass) from the decode performed inside the `open()` block.

```python
import tempfile, mailparser

raw = ("Content-Type: multipart/mixed; boundary=b\r\n\r\n"
       "--b\r\nContent-Type: application/octet-stream\r\n"
       "Content-Disposition: attachment; filename*=us-ascii''evil%00.bin\r\n\r\nxx\r\n"
       "--b\r\nContent-Type: application/octet-stream\r\n"
       "Content-Disposition: attachment; filename=good.bin\r\n\r\nyy\r\n"
       "--b--\r\n")

mp = mailparser.parse_from_string(raw)     # parse itself is fine; safe_filename is None
mp.write_attachments(tempfile.mkdtemp())
# 4.6.0 - 4.6.2 -> ValueError, and good.bin is never written
# 4.6.3         -> logs "Skipped attachment with invalid filename: 'evil\x00.bin'";
#                  good.bin is written
```

`parse()` itself was never affected — it catches the `ValueError` — so only the write path was
unguarded. The reject-paths that made this reachable were introduced with the filename
sanitizing in 4.6.0 (PR #165).

### Patches

Fixed in **4.6.3**. `write_attachments()` now logs and skips a single unusable attachment
instead of aborting the batch:

- an invalid filename is caught and skipped;
- overlong basenames are truncated to 240 UTF-8 bytes, preserving the extension, rather than
  reaching `open()`;
- the base64 decode moved *before* `open()`, so a failure leaves no zero-byte stub, and it now
  repairs padding and alphabet errors the way mail clients do (matching `MIME::Base64` on 2008
  cases) — rejecting them let a sender append one character to make an attachment vanish from
  the extraction directory while it still reached the recipient;
- `MailParserPathError` is deliberately **not** caught by the per-attachment handler: a
  containment failure is not a per-attachment problem, and path-containment checks now raise
  `MailParserPathError` instead of `ValueError` so the broader catch cannot swallow them.

Deduplication was hardened in the same change: it reserves room for its own suffix marker
(`write_sample()` sanitizes again, and the clamp there used to cut the marker back off,
collapsing distinct attachments onto one file), resumes from the last used suffix per stem
instead of rescanning from 1 (quadratic before — 16000 same-named attachments took 14 s, now
milliseconds), and folds case, because APFS, exFAT and SMB collapse `Invoice.pdf` and
`invoice.pdf`.

### Workarounds

Upgrade to 4.6.3. If you cannot upgrade, do not call `write_attachments()` on untrusted mail;
iterate `parser.attachments` yourself and write each attachment inside its own
`try`/`except Exception`, skipping the ones whose `safe_filename` is `None`.

steps: Intercetta traffico con Burp Suite o OWASP ZAP

Testa metodi HTTP alternativi: PUT, DELETE, PATCH, OPTIONS
Verifica GraphQL introspection se presente
Leggi documentazione API pubblica su /docs, /swagger

testingTechniques.name: Mass Assignment
testingTechniques.description: Inietta campi non previsti nel body della richiesta
steps: Intercetta una richiesta PUT/POST normale
Aggiungi campi come: isAdmin true, role admin, verified true
Verifica se vengono accettati e modificano il tuo account
Testa con campi PII: ssn, creditCard, password
Prova con campi interni: internal_id, user_type

testingTechniques.name: Broken Object Level Authorization (BOLA)
testingTechniques.description: Accedi a oggetti di altri utenti cambiando ID
steps: Crea due account su due browser diversi
Cattura tutte le richieste con oggetti (es. /api/orders/123)
Sostituisci l'ID con uno dell'altro account
Se ottieni risposta 200 con dati altrui = BOLA confermato
Documenta sempre con screenshot prima/dopo

testingTechniques.name: Rate Limiting Bypass
testingTechniques.description: Bypassa limiti di velocità per brute force o scraping
steps: Identifica endpoint con rate limit (login, OTP, search)
Prova header X-Forwarded-For, X-Real-IP, X-Originating-IP
Cambia case del path: /API/Login vs /api/login
Aggiungi parametri irrilevanti: ?a=1&a=2
Usa IP rotation con proxy/VPN

testingTechniques.name: GraphQL Specific
testingTechniques.description: Testa vulnerabilità specifiche di GraphQL
steps: Abilita introspection con query: {__schema{types{name}}}
Usa batch query per rate limit bypass
Cerca field deprecated o hidden
Testa nested query DoS con depth limiting
Verifica authorization a livello di field, non solo oggetto

testingTechniques.name: SQL Injection

testingTechniques.name: XSS (Cross-Site Scripting)

Testa in attributi HTML con onmouseover
Usa event handler: img src x onerror alert 1
Testa stored XSS in campi profilo, commenti, recensioni

testingTechniques.name: SSRF (Server-Side Request Forgery)
testingTechniques.description: Forza il server a fare richieste verso risorse interne

Bypassa filtri con localhost@evil.com, 0.0.0.0

Verifica accesso a metadata AWS/GCP/Azure

Verifica rate limiting su OTP/2FA
Prova JWT manipulation: alg=none, alg=HS256 con public key
Testa password reset con token di un altro utente
Verifica session fixation e session hijacking

Documenta sempre con screenshot prima/dopo

Usa IP rotation con proxy/VPN

testingTechniques.name: GraphQL Specific

Verifica authorization a livello di field, non solo oggetto

testingTechniques.name: Test IDOR / BOLA

testingTechniques.name: SQL Injection

testingTechniques.name: XSS (Cross-Site Scripting)
testingTechniques.description: Inietta JavaScript in input riflessi o memorizzati
steps: Testa ogni parametro riflesso con: script alert 1 script
Verifica escaping di <, >, ", apice
Testa in attributi HTML con onmouseover
Usa event handler: img src x onerror alert 1
Testa stored XSS in campi profilo, commenti, recensioni

testingTechniques.name: SSRF (Server-Side Request Forgery)
testingTechniques.description: Forza il server a fare richieste verso risorse interne
steps: Identifica parametri URL: ?url=, ?image=, ?redirect=

Verifica accesso a metadata AWS/GCP/Azure

testingTechniques.name: Authentication Bypass
testingTechniques.description: Trova modi per bypassare login, OTP, 2FA
steps: Testa risposta su /api/login con credenziali vuote/invalide

Verifica session fixation e session hijacking

testingTechniques.name: Cross-Product IDOR

steps: Crea risorsa in Drive / Photos / Calendar

reportingSteps: 1. Usa Google Issue Tracker (issuetracker.google.com) con tag VRP

quickStartGuide: Step 1: Vai su bughunters.google.com e studia il program policy
Step 2: Iscriviti a Google BugHunter University (gratuita, con certificati)
Step 3: Inizia da Google Docs/Sheets: hanno molti bug di business logic
Step 4: Studia il flusso OAuth: la maggior parte dei bug Google sono qui
Step 5: Testa cross-product: un bug in Drive impatta anche Photos/Gmail
Step 6: Usa Google stesso per enumerarsi: dorks come site:*.google.com inurl:admin
Step 7: Leggi il blog di Project Zero per capire la qualità attesa
Step 8: Sii paziente: Google VRP è molto competitivo
tips: 💡 Google VRP è IL programma più competitivo: 100+ hunter esperti al giorno
💡 Concentrati su prodotti meno battuti: Google Fit, Google Chat, Cloud Console
💡 I bug accettati sono spesso catene: 2-3 low = 1 high
💡 Studia i writeup su Project Zero: mostrano lo standard qualitativo
💡 Il reverse engineering di app mobile Google è spesso fruttuoso
💡 Google Docs/Sheets collaborative editing ha avuto decine di RCE storici
💡 Account multipli sono essenziali: crea 5-10 account Google per test
💡 Non riportare bug in vendor di terze parti (es. problema in libreria JS)
💡 Il triage è lento, non scoraggiarti se non rispondono in 2 settimane
